scholarships.name: Aker Cambridge Scholarship

source.rawText: Scholarship information The Aker Cambridge Scholarship is available to Masters and PhD applicants from Norway or with a strong link to Norway. The scholarship is tenable at any College of the University of Cambridge and in any subject. Offered in partnership with Anne Grete Eidsvig and Kjell Inge Røkkes Charitable Foundation for Education, Norway. Value University tuition fee (International rate). Annual maintenance (sufficient for a single person). Student visa. Student Immigration Health Surcharge. An economy airfare to the UK at the start of study, and an economy airfare from the UK to the student’s country of residence at the end of study, by the lowest cost available route. Conditions Successful applicants will have to agree to Aker Scholarship’s terms and conditions. How to apply To ensure that they are considered for this scholarship, applicants must follow both of the following steps: Apply direct to the Aker Scholarship in the year before that in which they wish to start their studies in Cambridge; AND Apply for admission to the University of Cambridge by the funding deadline specific to their course. Please refer to the Postgraduate Course Directory. For more information please visit our Postgraduate applicants page. Funding Partner: View Partner Profile Aker Cambridge Scholarship The Aker Scholarship was established in 2015 by the ‘Anne Grete Eidsvig and Kjell Inge Røkke Charitable Foundation for Education’ in cooperation with Aker ASA. The programme supports top Norwegian students so that they can learn from the best in the world, regardless of their family or financial situation. Scholarships are awarded to students in all fields of study. Its aim is to give talented and ambitious young Norwegian students the opportunity to gain knowledge, inspiration and experience by taking postgraduate degrees at the world’s leading universities.

source.rawText: Scholarship information The Bhutan King’s Scholarship is available to Masters applicants who are resident citizens of Bhutan. Conditions Applicants should show a firm commitment to return to work in Bhutan after completion of the degree. Priority will be given to those applying for courses within the fields of: Economics Education Engineering Environmental Studies International Relations Law Management Mathematics and Science Political Science Public Health and Medicine Public Policy How to apply No separate application is required for this scholarship, only the application for admission to the University of Cambridge, which must be submitted by the funding deadline specific to your course. Please refer to the Postgraduate Course Directory. For more information please visit our Postgraduate applicants page. Funding Partner: View Partner Profile Bhutan King’s Scholarship at the University of Cambridge The Kidu Foundation began with an incredible act of kindness. When natural disasters struck Bhutan in 2009, people from all over responded with an outpouring of donations – both money and supplies – to help those affected. This generosity was so overwhelming that it led to the creation of the Kidu Foundation. Today, the foundation works hand-in-hand with the Bhutanese government to tackle some of the country’s most important challenges. They focus on areas including education, rule of law and democracy, sustainable economic development and environmental and cultural protection. What makes this foundation special is its deep roots in Bhutan’s culture. The word ‘Kidu’ means ‘wellbeing’ – and taking care of people’s wellbeing has always been something special about Bhutan’s king

source.rawText: Scholarship information The Brockmann Cambridge Scholarship is available to Masters applicants from Mexico, in any subject except Master of Business, Executive Master of Business Administation and Global EMBA, Master of Finance and Executive Master of Accounting, which are not supported under this award. Conditions Applicants must have completed a four-year undergraduate degree in any field, terminating with a diploma, showing good academic progress. Agree to accept the Brockmann Foundation’s terms of support which require repayment of 30% of the Brockmann Foundation’s portion of the scholarship interest free on return to Mexico after completion of studies. source.rawText: Scholarship information This scholarship is available to Masters applicants who are citizens of Lebanon, Jordan, Palestine or Syria. It is tenable at any College. Funding Partner: View Partner Profile Bseisu-University of Cambridge Scholarship The mission of The Bseisu Foundation is to break down financial barriers that prevent talented young people in the Levant region – particularly Palestine, Syria, Lebanon and Jordan – from accessing higher education. They believe that the cornerstone of human development is empowering youth through access to education at the world’s best universities. With a primary focus on STEM degrees at the postgraduate level, they work with leading institutions such as the University of Cambridge, Oxford, Imperial College London and the London School of Economics to name a few. The programme expands into partnerships with the best universities in Malaysia and Palestine.

source.rawText: Scholarship information The Cambridge Australia Scholarships are available to Masters and PhD applicants from Australia in all subjects. They are tenable at any College of the University of Cambridge. Offered in partnership with Cambridge Australia Scholarships. Value Masters: Part-cost scholarship. PhD: Full-cost scholarship, covering: University tuition fee (International rate). Annual maintenance (sufficient for a single person). Contribution towards student Immigration Health Surcharge. Contribution towards travel. How to apply No separate application is required for this scholarship, only the application for admission to the University of Cambridge, which must be submitted by the funding deadline specific to your course. Please refer to the Postgraduate Course Directory. For more information please visit our Postgraduate applicants page. Funding Partner: View Partner Profile Cambridge Australia Scholarships Cambridge Australia Scholarships (CAS) is a not-for-profit organisation that provides scholarships for outstanding Australian graduates to undertake Masters and PhD degrees at the University of Cambridge. Since its establishment in the 1980s (as the Cambridge Australia Trust), over 350 scholarships have been awarded in partnership with the Cambridge Trust under a variety of schemes, many of them named after donors or eminent Australian alumni. CAS relies on the generosity of its donors, and all of its scholarships are funded by private philanthropic gifts. In recognition of its generosity in funding Australian students at Cambridge, in 2011 CAS was inducted into the University’s Guild of Benefactors. Cambridge Australia Scholarships are funded jointly by CAS and the Cambridge Trust, and are available to Australian applicants at Masters and PhD level.

source.rawText: Scholarship information The Cambridge Marshall PhD Scholarship is available to PhD applicants from the USA who are recipients of a two-year Marshall Scholarship. The scholarship funds the third year of a three-year PhD course in any subject excluding premium rate courses and is tenable at any College of the University of Cambridge. Offered in partnership with The Marshall Commission. See here for more information on Marshall Scholarships. Value University tuition fee (International rate). Annual maintenance (sufficient for a single person). Student visa. Student Immigration Health Surcharge. An economy airfare to the UK, and an economy airfare from the UK to the student’s country of residence, by the lowest cost available route Additional allowances: Transport allowance. Academic allowance. Leadership allowance. Other benefits up to £3,000 in excess of the maintenance. Conditions Applicants should be US citizens who are recipients of a two-year Marshall Scholarship which they intend to apply to fund a PhD course at the University of Cambridge. This scholarship is not available for the Doctor of Business course. How to apply To ensure that they are considered for this scholarship, applicants must follow both of the following steps: Be a recipient of a two-year Marshall Scholarship, for which a separate application is required; AND Apply for admission to the University of Cambridge by the funding deadline specific to their course (please refer to the Postgraduate Course Directory) and have a conditional offer of admission. For more information please visit our Postgraduate applicants page.
